synoptic.summary: The Pacific Northwest trough is moving east tonight. Showers end along the Wasatch Front this evening, and snow levels drop to the valley floors. High pressure builds over Utah on Saturday, bringing dry, clearing weather and light 150°–180° flow at the launches. Flow aloft is only 5–12 kt, so Saturday is the calm day of the run. The ridge moves east on Sunday. Ahead of Monday's system, flow aloft strengthens to 20–24 kt from 185°–207° at 3,400–5,200 ft above the POM landings, which is a mixing-down risk. On Monday a weaker storm system crosses. The forecast discussion is highly confident it arrives but uncertain on details. It brings a 32–50% shower chance with thunder at 2–4%, and the flow turns to 300°–340° by mid-afternoon. On Saturday and Sunday the flow stays at 120°–180° all day. The usual afternoon switch to 320°–360° is not forecast until Monday.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: Behind the exiting trough, high pressure is expected to be the dominant feature over Utah and southwest Wyoming this weekend. … There is high confidence in a storm system impacting the area on Monday. This will be weaker than the last few systems but is likely to bring accumulating snow to the mountains.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport read 1013.9 mb at 17:54 local Friday, up 7.6 mb since 05:54 (1006.3 mb), as the trough exits and high pressure builds. That favors Saturday. The ridge moves east Sunday, so expect pressure to fall into Monday ahead of the next system. The data does not reach that far yet.

observations.summary: These are Friday evening readings from 16:50–18:30 local, about 13 h before the first slot. With the trough moving out, the flow is backing toward 150°–170°. Salt Lake airport read 150°/5 kt with light rain at 18:30, South Valley Regional 170°/5 kt at 17:15, and Lehi 120°/10 kt G11 at 17:50. Spanish Fork showed 357°/3 kt and Provo was calm. The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no data. Alpine's newest reading (16:50) has a gust value only. All of this fits the forecast discussion's return to 150°–180° flow overnight.

d2-am.explanation: Saturday morning is the textbook POM South setup under building high pressure. Drainage from 170° at 7 kt (gusts 10–11 kt) loads the launch from 08:00. Flow aloft is light (≤12 kt), so mixing is no threat. Right at sunrise the forecast shows 230°, so wait until the sock settles on 160°–200°. Confidence is medium because the Point of the Mountain station returned no data and the readings are from Friday evening.

It would improve if the flow veers to 170°+ and the flow aloft comes in weaker.

d4-pm.explanation: Monday afternoon brings the switch to 300°–340° at only 4 kt (gusts to 8 kt), and the flow aloft is light. On wind alone this would be a go. But the system passing through gives a 47% shower chance until 16:00 and a small thunder risk, so it is marginal at best. The best odds are the last hour before sunset, when the shower chance falls to 13%. Confidence is low: this is three days out and timing is uncertain.
